conventions: τε is decided by rule 70's count of the English conjunctions the ASV wrote in the stretch, and the clause-seam 'and' counts. ACT.18.4 ἔπειθέν τε Ἰουδαίους καὶ Ἕλληνας → 'and persuaded Jews and Greeks' has two, so τε takes the seam 'and' introducing its clause and καί takes the one between the nouns, as rule 70's ἐλάλει τε καὶ συνεζήτει gives an 'and' to each; ACT.18.5 ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος → 'Silas and Timothy' has one, so that word is the καί's and τε is unrepresented; ACT.18.26 οὗτός τε has no answering καί and takes the 'and' written for it. Do not read the internal 'and' alone as 'the one English conjunction for the pair' and then mark the seam 'and' added under rule 98: a τε standing in that seam is the token it answers to.

ἀρχισυνάγωγος → 'ruler of the synagogue' is one unit headed on 'ruler' at ACT.18.8 and ACT.18.17: the compound denotes a person, 'ruler' is the word naming that referent, and 'synagogue' stands in a supplied prepositional complement rather than as the phrase's referring noun. Heading on 'synagogue' by analogy with rule 66's ἀρχιερεύς → 'chief priest' on 'priest' remains defensible and is the competing reading; the analogy is imperfect because there the second element names the person and here it does not.

A periphrastic εἰμί + participle is split by the English the ASV actually wrote, not joined into one unit. ACT.18.25 ἦν κατηχημένος → 'had been instructed' gives 'had been' to the copula and 'instructed' to the participle; ACT.18.7 ἦν συνομοροῦσα → 'joined hard' gives the whole English to the participle and leaves ἦν its own unrepresented unit, no English word answering to it separately. Rule 2 is what prefers the split and rule 94's count-of-English-words test is the shape of it. Joining the pair into one unit remains defensible, and a reference comparison will report the unrepresented copula as a disagreement.
report: Checked all 45 candidate lemma groups and, separately, the five `added` units the lemma table cannot see. No real split found: every difference is licensed by the Greek or by what the ASV wrote.

τε was the candidate worth the work. 18.4 (ἔπειθέν τε Ἰουδαίους καὶ Ἕλληνας → 'and persuaded Jews and Greeks') aligns τε to the clause-seam 'and'; 18.5 (ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος → 'Silas and Timothy') leaves it unrepresented. That is one analysis, not two: rule 70 counts the English conjunctions the ASV wrote in the stretch, and 18.4 has two while 18.5 has one, exactly as rule 70's own ἐλάλει τε καὶ συνεζήτει stands against ἐθνῶν τε καὶ βασιλέων. 18.26's τε has no answering καί and keeps the 'and' written for it. Recorded as a convention, because reading 'one English conjunction for the pair' off the internal 'and' alone would empty 18.4's τε and strand its clause 'and' as added.

The added/folded boundary is coherent. Both supplied locative 'there' units (18.11, 18.23) are added with no licensing token, while 18.26's supplied 'unto them' is folded because it realizes the προσ- preverb under rule 106. Every supplied juncture sits on the constituent it introduces (18.1, 18.2, 18.6, 18.7, 18.17, 18.18, 18.19, 18.22, 18.23, 18.24, 18.27); 18.28's 'and that' is added at an asyndetic seam between two adverbs both rendered as adverbs, which is rule 98 and not rule 88. 18.14's added 'that' subordinates a finite indicative (rule 86) where 18.5 and 18.28 fold 'that' onto an expanded infinitive (rule 85) — the Greek separates them, not the English.

Articles are uniform: before names and before determinerless nouns unrepresented throughout; rule 20's second arm gives the article a supplied possessive at 18.3, 18.6, 18.14 and 18.18, and the article is emptied wherever a genitive pronoun stands free. κεφαλή writes both halves of that contrast — 18.6 τὴν … ὑμῶν → 'your own heads' with the article empty, 18.18 τὴν → 'his' with no pronoun standing — and τῷ γένει → 'by race' is analysed identically at 18.2 and 18.24. Rule 106 is consistent across all thirteen compound verbs: the preverb particle rides inside the verb's unit, an expressed preposition takes the English preposition, a governed dative or genitive takes the case preposition where the ASV wrote a verb word (18.2, 18.10, 18.12, 18.14, 18.26), and an accusative or recast nominative object leaves it with the verb (18.17, 18.25).

Heads that recur are settled the same way in every verse: ἀρχισυνάγωγος → 'ruler' (18.8, 18.17), βῆμα → 'seat' (18.12, 18.16, 18.17), ἀποτάσσομαι → 'leave' (18.18, 18.21), οὗτος + generic noun → the demonstrative (18.13, 18.25), τούτων → 'these' (18.15, 18.17). The first of these is a genuine judgment against a live alternative and is logged.

BSB: all nine disagreements are documented convention differences and none is an error. Four are articles English realizes nowhere (18.10 the nominalizing article of τοῦ κακῶσαι, rule 61; 18.12 τῆς Ἀχαΐας and 18.13 τοὺς ἀνθρώπους, rule 23; 18.26 τοῦ θεοῦ, rules 23 and 21), two are articles a possessive displaces (18.6 τὴν κεφαλὴν ὑμῶν and 18.15 τοῦ νόμου, rule 20), and three are prepositions the ASV writes no word for (18.14 κατὰ λόγον recast as the subject 'reason', 18.15 καθ᾽ ὑμᾶς compressed into 'your own', 18.20 ἐπὶ πλείονα χρόνον → 'a longer time'), each rule 36's own case. Nothing changed to improve the rate.

Promotion considered and declined: the periphrastic εἰμί + participle split (18.7 ἦν unrepresented under a single 'joined'; 18.25 ἦν → 'had been') generalises, but it rests here on two units and I do not have the corpus contexts of εἰμί's unrepresented rows in hand, so it is logged as a convention rather than written into the contract.
